HOME AND DAILY LIFE LESSON · HOME AND DAILY LIFE · AGES 3–5 YEARS

Bathroom Routines — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches the bathroom as five actions with five songs: the singing does the sequencing, and the child runs the whole routine on melody alone.

What is this?

The bathroom routines are the verbs of the room: wash hands, brush teeth, wash face, take a bath, dry hands — done daily, in some order, forever.

What does it mean?

Routines live on rails, and songs are rails. A two-line tune with the words inside — bubbles, bubbles, scrub and rinse — will outlast any reminder a grown-up can give.

What does the child need to know?

You need the card and any sink. Invent the two-line songs together on the spot; familiar tunes (happy birthday speed) work better than clever ones.

Why this matters

Hand washing needs its twenty seconds — a song is the timer. Teeth need their two minutes — another song, longer. The music is not decoration; it is the mechanism.

What it teaches

Self-care sequences, timing by song (an early math sense), and the ownership of hygiene — the child who starts the song starts the routine.

Words to learn

wash handsbrush teethwash facetake a bathdry hands

Say this to your child

“"Bathroom routines — with the songs! Sing the hands song while the bubbles work, sing the teeth song while the brush runs. The music does the remembering."”

Step by step

  1. Show the card: "five jobs, five songs — let us write them."
  2. Hands song first, at the real sink: soap, bubbles, scrub, rinse — sing it twice through (that is the twenty seconds).
  3. Teeth song: up and down, front and back — long version, two minutes for the real brush.
  4. Face song at the wash: splish, tickle, done.
  5. Drying song to finish: towel, towel, dry dry dry — the forgotten half, now sung.

Look closer at the picture

On this card the words "Bathroom Routines" sit over five small scenes: hands under a running tap, a brush and toothpaste in a cup, hands splashing a face, a bubble-topped bath and hands drying on a towel rail.

Ask your child

"What song goes with the soap?" "How long do we brush?" (the whole teeth song) "What comes after washing — always?" (drying)

What your child can say or do

Your child might sing the hands song at every random sink, conduct the teeth song with the brush, or assign the drying song to every towel in the house.

Out in the real world

The songs travel: any sink, any campsite, any grandparent’s bathroom — the child starts singing and the washing happens on beat. Restrooms everywhere run on this.

Try it together

Song Swap: tonight the child composes a new line for one routine song and teaches it to you. Composer-led hygiene: the routine gets renewed by its owner.

Understanding check

Ask: "What do we sing while the soap bubbles?" (the hands song) "What is the forgotten half of washing?" (drying) "Who starts the songs?" (you do)

This lesson pairs with the Bathroom Routines flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Home and Daily Life.
